title: Numeric and String Enums
ques: Compare **Numeric Enums** and **String Enums** in TypeScript. Write examples of both and explain why string enums are generally preferred in production codebases.
explanation: String enums produce readable, meaningful serialization values in network logs and JSON payloads, whereas numeric enums serialize to opaque numbers and allow reverse-mapping quirks.

title: Partial and Required Utility Types
ques: Explain the functions of the built-in **`Partial<T>`** and **`Required<T>`** utility types. Write a code sample showing how `Partial` enables safe user profile update patches.
explanation: `Partial<T>` transforms every property in type `T` into an optional property, ideal for PATCH endpoints. `Required<T>` strips the `?` modifier, making every field mandatory.

title: Enforcing Immutability with Readonly Utility
ques: Demonstrate the use of the **`Readonly<T>`** utility type to create an immutable object configuration in TypeScript.
explanation: `Readonly<T>` maps over all keys of type `T` and prepends the `readonly` modifier, preventing accidental mutations at compile time.

title: Mapping Dictionaries with Record
ques: Explain how the **`Record<K, T>`** utility type creates structured object maps. Write a type definition that maps application roles (`admin`, `editor`, `viewer`) to permission lists.
explanation: `Record<K, T>` constructs an object type whose keys are taken from union `K` and whose values are of type `T`, ensuring exhaustive coverage of all designated keys.

title: Shaping Data with Pick and Omit
ques: Contrast **`Pick<T, K>`** and **`Omit<T, K>`**. Create a base `UserAccount` interface with sensitive fields and generate a public preview type using both utilities.
explanation: `Pick<T, K>` constructs a type by picking a specified set of keys from `T`. `Omit<T, K>` constructs a type by removing designated keys from `T`.

title: Union Filtering with Exclude and Extract
ques: Explain the conditional utility types **`Exclude<T, U>`** and **`Extract<T, U>`**. Provide code samples showing how each utility operates on union types.
explanation: `Exclude<T, U>` filters out assignable union members from `T`, while `Extract<T, U>` retains only those members of `T` that match `U`.
